notes: Hakra Ware culture (the Hakra phase) of the Ghaggar-Hakra valley, the contemporary of the Ravi phase. The page's dates are loose: 'the fourth millennium BCE', 'One estimate is 3500-3100/3000 BCE', 'Bhirrana material may be older, in the 8th millennium BCE' and the Hakra phase 'at least from early 6th to late 4th millennium B.C.'; 'contemporaneous with the early Harappan Ravi phase culture (3300-2800 BCE)'; Kot Diji is dated '3370 B.C. - 2900 B.C.'. The dossier takes the 3500-3000 estimate (confidence 2 for the year; the page offers no single date) and ignores the older Bhirrana dates, which the Mehrgarh page also reports ('Hakra Ware ... dated at a time bracket between 7380 and 6201 BCE' from charcoal samples) and which would make the culture older than the floor. Extent: named after the Hakra paleochannel; 'the earliest dated Hakra Ware is at Cholistan'; sites in Haryana (Bhirrana in Fatehabad district, Kunal, Girwas, Farmana, Rakhigarhi) and 'some Hakra Ware sites in Pakistani Punjab' reaching the Faisalabad area; Jalilpur near the Ravi. The page does not name Bahawalpur or Sirsa: Bahawalpur (100 km) stands in for Cholistan, Sirsa (90 km) for the Haryana sites, and Faisalabad (60 km, without the Harappa disc that the Indus dossier draws) for the Punjab sites, a placement (the gazetteer lacks Cholistan, Fatehabad and Bhirrana; names needed). Relations: the Indus Valley Civilization dossier (sa-01) draws Harappa, upper Sindh and Mehrgarh from 3300 and gains the Ghaggar-Hakra country, 'settled in the Kot Diji phase', from nobody in 2800; the Hakra dossier therefore ends in 3000 into nobody's land and the Indus gain follows 200 years later. Kot Diji 'follows' Hakra Ware on the page with no described link; Mehrgarh: 'Not stated'. No area figure.
